title: These 22-year-old billionaire Peter Thiel proteges pay professionals $2M a day to train the AI that could replace them
excerpt: Would you work for 22-year-olds who envision the future of white-collar work without humans?
content_html:
Robyn Tellefsen

Sun, July 26, 2026 at 3:10 AM PDT 8 min read

Moneywise and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue through links in the content below.

Doctors, lawyers, investment bankers and journalists are moonlighting as AI trainers. Are they securing their spot in an AI-fueled future or signing their death sentence? That depends on who you ask.

Mercor, a gig-work platform that provides top white-collar talent to AI labs like OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, has tens of thousands of such experts. According to a Bloomberg report, the company pays out more than $2 million per day to contractors, but some have called out an intrusive level of surveillance and being "treated like human cattle (1)."

Must Read

  • Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

  • JPMorgan still sees gold hitting $5,000/oz by Q4 — and savvy investors are protecting their wealth with a tax-advantaged Gold IRA. Learn more with a free guide from Priority Gold

  • The tax breaks in Trump's 'big beautiful bill' expire after 2028 — and experts say most people won't act in time. What to do before the window closes

While some are hailing AI training as the hot new version of gig work, others have called it a "scheme to misclassify workers," Bloomberg reports. The very nature of contractor work is independent, meaning employers cannot tell individuals when to work and how that work gets done.

Yet there are open cases regarding Mercor exercising the kind of control associated with an employer.

And, ironically, the founders, who are in their early 20s, have never had traditional corporate jobs.

The 23-year-old founders who hail from the Bay Area are Thiel Fellows — members of the billionaire investor Peter Thiel's program that provides $250,000 grants to young people who are skipping or quitting college (2). And they have become the youngest self-made billionaires.

CEO Brendan Foody, CTO Adarsh Hiremath and board chairman Surya Midha each have a roughly 22% stake in the company, Forbes estimates (3).

"It's definitely crazy," Foody told Forbes. "It feels very surreal. Obviously beyond our wildest imaginations, insofar as anything that we could have anticipated two years ago."

The startup is now in talks to raise $500 million at a valuation that could double its $10 billion worth in less than a year (4).

Mercor did not immediately respond to Moneywise's request for comment.

Who really benefits from training AI?

Sundeep Peechu, managing partner at the VC firm Felicis Ventures, which led Mercor's previous funding rounds, commented on the category in the Bloomberg article.

医生、律师、投资银行家和记者都兼职做人工智能培训师。 他们是在人工智能驱动的未来中保住自己的位置，还是签署死刑判决？ 这取决于你问的是谁。

Mercor 是一个零工平台，为 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Meta 等人工智能实验室提供顶级白领人才，拥有数万名此类专家。 据彭博社报道，该公司每天向承包商支付超过 200 万美元，但一些承包商称其监控程度为侵入性，并“像人牛一样对待 (1)”。

必读

  • 杰夫·贝索斯 (Jeff Bezos) 支持一个平台，让任何人都可以以低至 100 美元的价格投资出租房屋——无需真正成为房东即可像房东一样积累财富的 6 种方法
  • 摩根大通仍然预计金价到第四季度将达到 5,000 美元/盎司，而精明的投资者正在通过税收优惠的黄金 IRA 来保护自己的财富。 通过 Priority Gold 的免费指南了解更多信息
  • 特朗普“美丽大法案”中的税收减免将于 2028 年到期，专家表示大多数人不会及时采取行动。 窗口关闭之前可以做什么

据彭博社报道，虽然一些人称赞人工智能培训是零工工作的热门新版本，但另一些人则称其为“错误分类工人的计划”。 承包商工作的本质是独立的，这意味着雇主无法告诉个人何时工作以及如何完成工作。

然而，还有一些关于 Mercor 行使与雇主相关的控制权的公开案例。

讽刺的是，两位 20 岁出头的创始人从未从事过传统的企业工作。

来自湾区的 23 岁创始人是 Thiel Fellows，他们是亿万富翁投资者 Peter Thiel 项目的成员，该项目为逃学或退学的年轻人提供 25 万美元的助学金 (2)。 他们已成为最年轻的白手起家的亿万富翁。

据《福布斯》估计，首席执行官 Brendan Foody、首席技术官 Adarsh Hiremath 和董事会主席 Surya Midha 各持有该公司约 22% 的股份 (3)。

“这绝对是疯狂的，”福迪告诉福布斯。 “感觉非常超现实。 显然这超出了我们最疯狂的想象，这是我们两年前所能预料到的。”

该初创公司目前正在洽谈融资 5 亿美元，其估值可能在不到一年的时间里使其 100 亿美元的价值翻一番 (4)。

Mercor 没有立即回应 Moneywise 的置评请求。

谁真正从训练人工智能中受益？

风险投资公司 Felicis Ventures 的管理合伙人 Sundeep Peechu 在彭博社的文章中评论了这一类别，该公司领导了 Mercor 之前的几轮融资。
